A static website: the page is `site/index.html`, its styles are in `site/css/`, its scripts in `site/js/` and its images in `site/assets/`.

- `npm start` serves the site on http://127.0.0.1:$PORT (the `PORT` variable is set).

content.text:
I've only partly fixed it: the visual test still fails on both desktop and phone, and I couldn't find the cause of what's left.

**Fixed:** the "Send Message" button had turned blue. Its disabled background in `site/css/styles.css` (line 2860, `--bs-btn-disabled-bg`) was `#0037ff`, and I changed it back to `#ffc800`. The button now matches the approved screenshot.

**Still different:** the remaining differences are in the text, not the layout. Text in the new render is about 0.3–0.7% narrower than in the approved screenshot, and the 1px offsets run through headings and body copy all the way down the page.

The visible effect is in the Services section, where the paragraph now fits "dicta" on the third line. The approved version wraps it onto the fourth.

The mismatch is about 28,000 pixels on desktop and 22,000 on phone, down from about 36,000 on desktop before the button fix.

I tried these, and none of them reduced the mismatch:
- font kerning and text-rendering settings
- other font families
- small letter-spacing and font-size nudges

The rendered font is Inter in every case. The only other lead is that `site/index.html` has empty `<!-- Font Awesome -->` and `<!-- Google fonts-->` sections with no links under them. Offline, those links wouldn't load anyway, so I can't confirm they're involved.

If you can tell me what the last change touched (fonts, the head of `index.html`, or something else), I can narrow it down. If the text difference is just a rendering drift on this machine, the baseline screenshots would need regenerating. I haven't done that, because it would hide a real regression if there is one.

`site/css/styles.css` is the only file I changed, and I haven't committed anything.

STATUS: NOT DONE
